candidates.evidence: Three measured Raman bands at 155.70, 299.57 and 354.10 cm-1 (532 nm, 295 K). The data are consistent with a layered crystal only in the weak sense that the bands are narrow (FWHM 5-9 cm-1). I found no reference mode list in the folder or in the literature search that matches these three positions, so no specific material can be named.

hint_reasoning: The material hint is null, so this is an identify task. I could not match the three bands to any reference. A literature search by material concept (layered oxyhalide Raman modes; InOCl Raman) returned no Raman spectrum for InOCl. The results were for BiOCl lattice dynamics, Bi-oxychalcogenides, MoTe2, MoO3 and PbFCl, and I did not read their mode tables, so I cite none of them. The reference-mode scripts and material notes in the skill directory are outside this folder and were not used, per the folder restriction.

artifacts.type: cosmic-ray spike, single point at 897.47 cm-1, 9238 counts, about 6x the neighbouring points (~1500). Replaced by the mean of its two neighbours before fitting. Not reported as a peak.

limits: No reference: I could not identify the material. The three bands are measured, but nothing in the folder or the literature I could reach gives their assignment. Any named material would be a guess.

Literature search: no Raman spectrum or mode table for InOCl was found. Searches returned unrelated materials (MoTe2, MoO3, Bi-oxychalcogenides, BiOCl lattice dynamics), and I did not read their mode tables. The iopic-bond tool failed (VALENCY_BOND_TOKEN not set), so its figure search was unavailable.
The folder path mentions a material name. I did not use it as evidence, since the data do not confirm it and I found no reference Raman data for it.

Data quality: the point-to-point noise is about 240 counts against a 6000-count band, and a fluorescence-like background slopes from ~3000 counts at 60 cm-1 to ~1000 at 1100 cm-1. Peak positions and FWHMs come from Lorentzian fits on a linear background over 100-420 cm-1 (residual RMS 241 counts, equal to the noise). Position uncertainties are fit statistics only (0.07, 0.47, 0.23 cm-1); no Si calibration was available to add calibration error.

No bands above noise were found in 420-1100 cm-1. Bumps in a 5-point-binned spectrum reached about 3.6 sigma at ~936 cm-1 and 3.0 sigma at ~1073 cm-1. With about 20 candidate bumps and a crude cubic background, these are not significant, so I did not report them.

The spectrum covers 60-1100 cm-1 with 0.8 cm-1 sampling, so the lowest acoustic and ultra-low modes below 60 cm-1 cannot be checked. No polarization or angle series was given, so polarization classes and irreps cannot be assigned.

At 532 nm, resonance with an exciton or electronic transition could enhance some bands and suppress others. I cannot judge that without a reference, and it does not change the lack of an identification.

What would settle it: the chemical composition (EDS or XPS) or the diffraction pattern, and a reference Raman spectrum of the candidate material at 532 nm. With those, the three positions can be compared directly with calculated or measured modes.
